R256-001 CLOSED. No blocking runtime correctness defect found in the delta.
The guard metrics now use old_guard (size plus idle) and new_guard
(disposition), not estimated cache warmth. Unknown-TTL warnings count
toward stopped-warm even without a known TTL. The two new Vitest cases
exercise the Python implementation and cover the original small-seat
misclassification, warning accounting, policy replay and boundaries.

Independent aggregation of the previously saved 13,404 metadata rows
(9,402 decided), without another live-store/transcript scan, agrees with
the corrected guard results and performance's final-head command run:

Guard metric                            Before       Shipped Warn
Clear, actually cold                       970                710
  of which large                           265                  5
Refused or warned, actually warm              4                 56
Refused                                    124                124
Warned                                       0                312

The 56 warm flags now comprise four refusals and 52 warnings. Under
RefuseAt 100/150/200, warm refusals are 56/31/14 and total refusals
436/357/296; these match independent aggregation and the corrected
note at governance e94ab1e73bfb1763d65f9075abcfb428ad3644a8.

Important meaning: Warn still ALLOWS 265 actually-cold large deliveries,
260 with warnings and five silently. The change removes silence, not the
cost of those permitted wakes. No 128M-token saving is claimed by this
review under the shipped default.

Policy boundaries and action consumers

Source inspection of cold_wake.rs:260-298 and the CI cases agree:
- Within the hour ceiling and below the known TTL, every option is clear.
- At the TTL, Warn warns, RefuseAt 100 refuses, and 150/200 warn.
- At 1.5x and 2x, the corresponding RefuseAt refuses inclusively.
- Idle strictly greater than 60 minutes refuses under every option,
  even for a longer TTL. At exactly 60 minutes, Warn still warns when
  the TTL has elapsed; RefuseAt acts on its own threshold. Thus a 1h
  TTL at exactly 60m is refused under 100 but warned under Warn/150/200.
- Unknown TTL is clear at exactly five minutes, warns after five
  through the hour, and refuses after the hour. Small and busy seats
  retain their previous admission behavior.

The Rust table tests every policy around its transition points; the
Python regression additionally pins exact TTL, 1.5x/2x and unknown-TTL
boundaries. This is source plus exact-head CI evidence, not a local run.

Force still requires a nonblank reason and audits Cold overrides before
delivery. A short-TTL send that now returns Warn no longer needs force;
its normal receipt contains the warning rather than a forced-Cold audit.
The unknown-TTL warning path and its roster/state presentation are intact.

cache_known/is_warm are unchanged: FYI flush and revive --cheap continue
to require known, non-table TTL evidence inside the real lifetime.
Idle nudge still admits only Clear|Busy at idle_nudge.rs:362-363:
Warn does NOT wake the seat. The change from Refuse to Warn therefore
does not loosen that admission. HTTP override/action wiring is unchanged.

Cost/security scope

The policy delta is pure, bounded arithmetic and matching: no new
per-send launch, read, loop, timer or poll. Warn no longer enters the
Cold-only stale-working probe for a short-TTL as-idle result. The test
adds two on-demand Python subprocesses to Vitest, not the daemon.
Fixtures contain synthetic token/time facts and no real seats, account
names, message bodies or credentials. Wire shape and TTL sources are
unchanged from round 1. No edits to fleet_report* or prompt-cache-cost.md.

Performance alone ran the final on-demand audit smoke: exit 0,
9.85s wall, 5.47 CPU-seconds, 187,613,184 bytes peak RSS, zero swaps.
Its guard/replay totals match the independent saved-row aggregation.
This is the before-window smoke, not the after-deploy audit.
